newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends down $2.25, Brent 11 cts lower.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends down $2.25, Brent 11 cts lower.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures closed down $2.25 a tonne in thin trade on Monday, pushed lower by weaker NYMEX heating oil and gasoline, traders said.
Front-month IPE March gas oil last traded at $160.25, 75 cents off the low, after touching a high of $163.75 driven by an open arb to Singapore.
"People are just looking for any excuse to get rid of gas oil. There is absolutely no demand," a trader said. "We needed a sustained long, cold spell and neither we nor the Americans have had one."
The contract bounced off support at $159.50.
But some traders saw it testing $150 a tonne in the longer term, a front month level not seen since October 1995.

April Brent was trading down 11 cents at $18.74 a barrel at 1750 GMT, two cents of its session low. "There's no news out there. (NYMEX) gasoline is seen as the support for the market so when that goes down the rest follows," one said.
April NYMEX unleaded gasoline last traded down 0.76 cents at 61.70 cents a gallon. April heating oil was down 64 cents at 52.80 cents a gallon.
The crude futures market had been expected to correct upwards on Monday following Friday's substantial losses.
But brokers were now looking for a further downward move with next support on the prompt Brent contract seen at $18.67 a barrel.
"There's been a treble bottom there and that should be quite good support. We are still looking for a correction but when it will happen is a bit of a lottery," another broker said.
